title: India highlights its Science-based advances in Snow Leopard Conservation including Population Estimation, Radio Telemetry and Genetic Analysis, at Moscow Roundtable Meeting
body_text:
India participated in the Russian-Indian Roundtable Meeting on Snow Leopard Study and Conservation, held on 26.08.2026, at the A.N. Severtsov Institute of Ecology and Evolution of the Russian Academy of Sciences in Moscow, Russia. The meeting was organised within the framework of the Partnership Agreement between the Interregional Association ‘Irbis’ and the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA), signed in December 2025, with the objective of strengthening international cooperation in snow leopard research and conservation.
The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India, delegation highlighted the country’s progress in the snow leopard conservation agenda through evolving science-based initiatives. Officials from the Wildlife Institute of India (WII) elaborated on advances in snow leopard population estimation, radio telemetry and genetic analysis, underscoring the growing role of scientific tools in strengthening conservation efforts.
The meeting also brought together representatives of the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment of the Russian Federation, A.N. Severtsov Institute of Ecology and Evolution of the Russian Academy of Sciences, Moscow Zoo, Rosprirodnadzor and leading experts in the field of snow leopard research and conservation. The Indian delegation participated in the Roundtable and thematic discussions focused on advancing collaborative approaches for conservation and scientific study of the species.
The Roundtable provided an important platform for India and international partners to exchange knowledge and experiences and to strengthen cooperation in snow leopard research, monitoring and conservation.

enrichment.summary: India participated in the Russian-Indian Roundtable Meeting on Snow Leopard Study and Conservation, held on 26 August 2026 in Moscow under the framework of a December 2025 Partnership Agreement between the 'Irbis' Association and the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA). The Indian delegation, including officials from the Wildlife Institute of India, presented India's scientific advances in snow leopard population estimation, radio telemetry, and genetic analysis. The meeting brought together Russian environmental bodies, research institutions, and experts to discuss collaborative conservation and monitoring approaches.
enrichment.context:
Snow leopards are found across the high-altitude Himalayan and trans-Himalayan regions of India and are listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act and Appendix I of CITES. India's Project Snow Leopard, launched in 2009, and periodic national population assessments (such as SPAI - Snow Leopard Population Assessment in India) form the backbone of its conservation science, which was showcased at this meeting. The International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA), launched by India in 2023 to promote conservation of seven big cat species including the snow leopard, provides the institutional umbrella for such international scientific cooperation, reflecting India's growing role in global wildlife diplomacy.

This release is essentially a report on India's participation in an international scientific roundtable rather than an announcement of new policy, funding, or conservation outcomes, limiting its direct examinability despite touching on relevant institutions like IBCA and WII.
